content.thinking: Checking webhook listeners to verify new events are forwarded.

Read tokens are open to any role. Write tokens require member or higher access.

I'll add permission actions for API tokens so `assertCan` can throw the codebase's `PermissionDeniedError`. This replaces direct role checks.

A PermissionDeniedError will be thrown.

Permission actions must be added to ROLE_MATRIX. "api_token:write" requires the member role. Listing own tokens needs no permission beyond tenant scope. Admin is only needed for listing other users' tokens.

Revoke actions will require admin or ownership escalation. A new api_token resource kind with orgId and userId will support ownership checks. The permission matrix will use "api_token:create_write" for members and "api_token:manage_others" for admins.

The api_token resource carries orgId and userId. assertCan will be called unconditionally for all token operations, including listing own tokens. Members pass the create_write check. Admins pass manage_others for other users. Viewers are blocked by both checks.

Revoke own tokens will use ownership escalation on the revoke action. Revoke other users' tokens requires admin. Listing another user's tokens will use a separate "api_token:manage" check without ownership escalation, since only admins can list other users' tokens.
An exhaustive permissions matrix test exists.

Adding permission actions is safe for the matrix test. The test uses the issue resource for all actions and only checks role rank, not resource kind match.

Cross-tenant access uses the organization resource. Unknown domains default to organization for api_token permissions. I will add api_token:write for members and api_token:administer for admins. List and revoke own will skip permission checks beyond tenant scope. Platform staff permissions are not specified.

The input type uses z.input to preserve the raw string before schema transforms. The name field is trimmed and limited to 80 characters. Scope is an enum and expiresInDays is a positive integer up to 365 days. The service validates input with schema.parse and throws ZodError on failure. Token secrets use a tfk_ prefix plus random characters. The expiration date is calculated from the creation time plus the configured number of days.

lastUsedAt and revokedAt start as null. A user may hold at most five usable tokens; creating a sixth fails immediately. The list returns newest first and includes revoked and expired tokens for the actor or an admin for another user. Revoking one's own token succeeds, while revoking another requires admin or owner. Authentication hashes the secret, resolves the role at call time, and updates lastUsedAt only on success.

A member-removed listener will revoke all of that member's tokens and audit the action. It must be registered in registerEventHandlers so tests can activate it. The listener reuses the payload actorId, which may be null.

The member-removed listener will revoke tokens directly via the repository layer instead of calling revokeApiToken. This avoids redundant permission checks and extra emits. It writes the revocation to the database and emits api_token.revoked immediately. The removeMember emit waits for this handler to finish so the audit record is written before the service call resolves.

Authentication will check organization deletion by verifying that archivedAt is set. If the organization row is missing, it is treated as deleted. A user who is not an active member, including archived or suspended members, will also be treated as deleted.

Authentication will resolve the actor and check organization deletion separately. Read access grants viewer role even if the member is owner; write access uses the member's actual role. The stored hash is never returned.

The api_token.created event carries tokenId, name, and scope. The api_token.revoked event carries tokenId. Activity listeners record these with subject kind api_token. Metadata must omit the secret and hash. The Drizzle enum for subject_kind needs to include api_token for consistency even though SQLite may not enforce a CHECK constraint.

Repository methods will include listByUser, findById, findByHash, countUsable, revoke, touchLastUsed, and listActiveForUser. The mapper must strip the hash from stored tokens. Index exports are needed for services, schemas, types, and the database schema. Activity labels require exhaustive coverage of the new actions to avoid compile errors.

Token IDs will be plain ULID strings rather than branded types. Expiration checks use strict greater-than comparisons against UTC ISO timestamps. The expiry date is computed by adding the configured number of days in milliseconds to the creation time.

Implementing all files now. Checking the search service for an exhaustive event list that could break compilation.

Updating the activity subject kind Drizzle enum to include api_token. Adding registerApiTokenListeners to the event registry so member removal handlers are wired automatically. Also considering revoking tokens directly inside removeMember as a fallback.

Revolving tokens only in the event listener avoids double-auditing. The emit awaits, so the pipeline stays clean and matches the spec.

The member.removed event may carry a null actorId, so the audit actor is always the remover. Bulk revocation emits one api_token.revoked event per token. The unrevoked list query filters by org and user with a null revokedAt check. Revocation sets revokedAt only if it is currently null. Expired tokens remain revoked. Other organizations are unaffected because the query scopes by orgId. Authentication updates lastUsedAt for the matched row only when the token is valid and not expired; failed attempts skip the update. Unknown hashes return null. Expiration is checked by comparing ISO strings.

Token expiration is checked with `expiresAt <= toIsoTimestamp(new Date())`, including exact matches. Usable tokens must have a null revokedAt and an expiresAt in the future. Results are ordered by newest first using descending createdAt and id. The new type will be exported from types/index.

I will avoid updating the large manifest unless tests require it.

I'll add new permission actions to handle viewer write errors. The nav.ts switch doesn't need changes. I'll revoke tokens when members are removed from the API token service. Create operations will validate schema and scope first, then check limits, then write. If the limit is reached nothing gets stored. List operations will start with org scope checks.

List queries default to the actor's own userId. A different userId requires admin permission. Revoke finds the token and checks scope, then verifies ownership or admin rights before marking revokedAt and emitting. Authenticate has no actor scope. Staff may create write tokens; viewers may not. Zod validation will catch invalid expiresInDays types.

Token names will be trimmed and validated between one and eighty characters. The schema will reuse the existing orgIdSchema. I'll export the input type, schema, and registerApiTokenListeners from the service file. Activity listeners will handle token creation and revocation events. Metadata for created tokens will include scope and name; revoked tokens will include a reason. No secrets will appear in summaries.

The member.removed handler will use the actorId from the removal event to record the revocation. It lists all unrevoked tokens for that user and organization, then marks them revoked with a current timestamp.

The handler will still revoke tokens and emit audit records even when the removal actorId is null. It will use the envelope helper for the event payload. Nested emit calls are safe because each call awaits current handlers before proceeding.

Event payloads will not include the token hash. The repository revoke method returns the updated row, and the service only calls it when the token is still unrevoked. Token counts are computed with a SQL count query. The api_tokens table stores id, org_id, user_id, name, scope, token_hash, prefix, expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at, created_at, and updated_at. Unique and composite indexes on token_hash and org_id plus user_id will be added via migration. The schema will be exported from the index file.

The client must re-export the schema so `apiTokens` is importable from `@/server/db`. Timestamps will follow the webhooks pattern: `updatedAt` updates on revoke and `lastUsed`, and inserts set `updatedAt` equal to `createdAt`. The domain type omits `updatedAt` and the hash. `id` stays a plain string, while `orgId` and `userId` remain branded, and `scope` uses the `ApiTokenScope` enum.
